name: ibu-adult-verbatim
q: What is the usual adult dose of ibuprofen?

sources.title: Ibuprofen
sources.text: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, fever and inflammation. It is sold over the counter as 200 mg tablets and as a liquid for children. This section is for adults and children over 12. The usual dose is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Do not take more than 1,200 mg in 24 hours without a doctor's advice. Children under 12 need a dose based on their weight. For children, the dose is 5 to 10 mg per kg every 6 to 8 hours. Children should not be given more than 40 mg per kg in a day. Take ibuprofen with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Do not take ibuprofen if you have a stomach ulcer. People with asthma should only use ibuprofen if they have taken it before without problems. Avoid ibuprofen from 20 weeks of pregnancy unless a doctor advises it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is nearly time for the next one. Stop taking it and get medical help at once if you vomit blood or pass black stools.

reply: ANSWER: The usual dose is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours [1].

name: baikal-depth-verbatim
q: How deep is Lake Baikal?

sources.title: Lake Baikal
sources.text: Lake Baikal is a rift lake in southern Siberia, Russia. It is the deepest lake in the world, with a maximum depth of 1,642 m. It is also the oldest lake, at an estimated 25 to 30 million years. The lake holds about 23,600 cubic kilometres of water, roughly 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. Lake Baikal is 636 km long and up to 79 km wide. More than 300 rivers flow into Lake Baikal. Only one river, the Angara, flows out of it. The lake freezes over from January to May. The ice can be more than 1 m thick. The nerpa, or Baikal seal, is found only in Lake Baikal. Most of the lake's animal species are found nowhere else on Earth. In winter, roads are marked out across the ice, except where warm springs keep it thin. The water is so clear that objects can be seen at a depth of 40 m in spring.

On weekdays, tram 28 runs every 10 to 12 minutes. At weekends, tram 28 runs every 15 minutes. A single ticket bought on board costs 3.10 euros. A Viva Viagem card brings the fare down to 1.80 euros. Pickpockets are common on crowded trams, so keep bags closed and in front of you. The metro has four lines. The metro runs from 6:30 a.m. to 1 a.m. every day. The ferry to Cacilhas leaves from Cais do Sodre every 10 to 20 minutes during the day. The last ferry leaves at 9 p.m. on Sundays and at 11 p.m. on other days. Taxis are cheap by European standards. Ride-hailing apps are widely used. Free guided walks leave the Praca do Comercio every weekday at 10 a.m. Do not board tram 28 in Alfama in summer if you want a seat.

sources.title: Hanoi for visitors
sources.text: In Hanoi, motorbikes far outnumber cars. To cross the street, walk slowly and steadily. Do not stop or run suddenly when crossing. Drivers will steer around you if they can predict where you are going. Book taxis through an app or a known company. Unofficial taxis may overcharge. Street food stalls are usually safe if they are busy and cook food in front of you. Tap water is not safe to drink. Drink bottled or boiled water. The Old Quarter is closed to motor traffic on weekend evenings. Most museums are closed on Mondays.

name: bike-levers-verbatim
q: How do I get the tyre off the rim?

sources.title: Fixing a flat bicycle tyre
sources.text: Step 1: Shift to the smallest rear sprocket and open the brake quick release. Step 2: Open the wheel's quick release lever and remove the wheel. Step 3: Use two tyre levers to lift one side of the tyre off the rim. Do not use a screwdriver, which can tear the tube. Step 4: Pull out the inner tube and find the hole by pumping it up and listening for air. Step 5: Run your fingers carefully around the inside of the tyre to find and remove whatever caused the puncture. Step 6: Roughen the area around the hole with sandpaper and spread a thin layer of glue. Wait about 5 minutes until the glue is dry to the touch. Step 7: Press the patch on firmly and hold it for at least 1 minute. Step 8: Put a little air in the tube and fit it back inside the tyre. Push the tyre back onto the rim with your thumbs. Step 9: Inflate the tyre to the pressure printed on its sidewall, usually between 40 and 65 psi for a hybrid bike. Never ride with the quick release open.

sources.title: Fixing a flat bicycle tyre
sources.text: Step 1: Shift to the smallest rear sprocket and open the brake quick release. Step 2: Open the wheel's quick release lever and remove the wheel. name: frost-rewarm-verbatim
q: How do I rewarm frostbitten fingers?

sources.title: Frostbite
sources.text: Frostbite is damage to skin and tissue caused by freezing. It most often affects the fingers, toes, nose and ears. It can occur at air temperatures below 0 °C (32 °F), and much faster in wind. Move the person somewhere warm before rewarming. Do not rub the affected area or massage it with snow. Rewarm frostbitten skin in warm water at 37 to 39 °C (99 to 102 °F) for 15 to 30 minutes. Do not use a heater, a fire or a hot water bottle to rewarm the skin, since numb skin burns easily. If the skin could freeze again, do not thaw it until the person reaches safety. Give pain relief such as ibuprofen as the skin thaws. Get medical help for anything but the mildest frostbite. At −20 °C with a wind of 30 km/h, exposed skin can freeze in about 30 minutes.

name: kettle-three-steps

sources.title: Descaling a kettle
sources.text: To descale a kettle with vinegar: Step 1: Unplug the kettle and let it cool. Step 2: Fill it half full with equal parts white vinegar and water. Step 3: Bring the mixture to the boil and leave it for 1 hour. Step 4: Pour the mixture away and rinse the kettle with clean water. Step 5: Boil a full kettle of clean water and pour it away twice, to remove the taste of vinegar. Do not use bleach in a kettle. For heavy scale, repeat steps 2 to 4. Lemon juice or citric acid can be used instead of vinegar.

sources.text: Heat stroke is a medical emergency in which the body temperature rises above 40 °C (104 °F). Call emergency services at once. Move the person to a cool place and remove extra clothing. Cool the person quickly with cold water, wet towels or ice packs on the neck, armpits and groin. Do not give the person anything to drink if they are confused. sources.title: Frostbite
sources.text: Frostbite is damage to skin and tissue caused by freezing. It most often affects the fingers, toes, nose and ears. It can occur at air temperatures below 0 °C (32 °F), and much faster in wind. Move the person somewhere warm before rewarming. Do not rub the affected area or massage it with snow. Rewarm frostbitten skin in warm water at 37 to 39 °C (99 to 102 °F) for 15 to 30 minutes. Do not use a heater, a fire or a hot water bottle to rewarm the skin, since numb skin burns easily. If the skin could freeze again, do not thaw it until the person reaches safety. Give pain relief such as ibuprofen as the skin thaws. Get medical help for anything but the mildest frostbite. At −20 °C with a wind of 30 km/h, exposed skin can freeze in about 30 minutes.

name: hanoi-cross-verbatim
q: How do I cross the street in Hanoi?

sources.title: Hanoi for visitors
sources.text: In Hanoi, motorbikes far outnumber cars. To cross the street, walk slowly and steadily. Do not stop or run suddenly when crossing. It stretches for over 2,300 km. The reef can be seen from outer space. Water temperatures on the reef range from 23 °C in winter to 29 °C in summer. Coral bleaching happens when the water stays too warm for too long. Major bleaching events occurred in 1998, 2002, 2016, 2017 and 2020. Stinger suits are recommended from November to May, when box jellyfish are found near the coast. Do not touch or stand on coral. Most tours leave from Cairns or Port Douglas.
